title: Livestream: Lindsay Clancy murder trial continues with her psychiatric treatment in the spotlight
author: Abby Patkin
bullets: Lindsay Clancy is charged with first-degree murder for the deaths of her three children in Duxbury in January 2023.
Clancy raises an insanity defense, citing postpartum mental illness, while prosecutors claim she planned the killings.
Testimony focuses on Clancy's psychiatric treatment, with discussions on her medication and a possible bipolar disorder diagnosis.

title: Acton teen located after police discover two dead in home
author: Ross Cristantiello
bullets: Police found a woman and a teen boy dead in a Martha Lane home in Acton.
Authorities located 17-year-old Arjun Aravind, previously sought after the discovery of two bodies in the home he shared.
A green Honda Accord linked to the incident was found in Wayland; investigation is ongoing.

title: Q&A: Boston’s nightlife czar says the city is just getting started
author: Beth Treffeisen
bullets: Corean Reynolds, Boston's nightlife czar, oversees efforts to boost the city's 24-hour economy, expanding late-night venues and social districts.
Boston's temporary social districts, allowing outdoor drinking and extended hours, increased business revenue, with no complaints reported.
Reynolds aims to continue policy adjustments, including less restrictive alcohol regulations and improved late-night transportation options.

title: Recent homes sales in Greater Boston (Aug. 12)
author: The Boston Globe
bullets: A condo at 46 Beacon St. in Boston sold for $18 million, the highest reported sale in the article.
In Acton, 16 Chestnut St. #5 condo was purchased for $1,190,000.
11 Lillian Road in Acton, a one-family ranch, sold for $540,000.

title: Nearly 50 children recovered during anti-human trafficking operation in Greater Boston during the World Cup, officials say
author: Samantha Genzer
bullets: 48 missing and endangered children recovered in Massachusetts during multi-agency anti-trafficking operation in the World Cup.
Operation Yellow Card involved U.S. Marshals, Massachusetts State Police, and Boston Police, targeting child exploitation and trafficking.
Recovered children, aged 12-17, were reunited with families or connected to welfare services; further investigations are underway.

title: Why Patriots rookie Caleb Lomu isn’t fretting over up-and-down training camp
author: Conor Ryan
bullets: Caleb Lomu, Patriots rookie tackle, experiences both wins and struggles in 2026 training camp drills.
Lomu, picked 28th in the 2026 NFL Draft, alternates roles between left and right tackle during practice.
Veteran Morgan Moses mentors Lomu, advising him to focus on incremental skill improvements during training.

title: 12-year-old seriously injured after train surfing Red Line, Transit Police says
author: Samantha Genzer
bullets: A 12-year-old boy was seriously injured after attempting to train surf on an MBTA Red Line car in Dorchester.
The incident occurred around 1 a.m. at the JFK/UMass station; the boy sustained a serious head injury.
Authorities are investigating the incident and warn of the severe dangers of train surfing, which has historical precedence.

title: Adam Vinatieri says there’s ‘no animosity’ with Patriots, Bill Belichick after Hall-of-Fame speech
author: Conor Ryan
bullets: Adam Vinatieri, in his Hall of Fame speech, joked about Bill Belichick and former teammates, emphasizing there was no ill intent.
Vinatieri clarified on WEEI that his speech jokes weren't meant to express animosity towards the Patriots or Belichick.
Robert Kraft and Bill Belichick missed the Hall of Fame ceremony due to logistical issues, not as a result of any bad blood.

title: New Bedford temporarily suspends use of Flock as the surveillance cameras come under increased scrutiny
author: Samantha Genzer
bullets: New Bedford suspended Flock camera use amid privacy and oversight concerns following internal investigations and an officer's administrative leave.
Flock Safety cameras, used since 2024, are under review for their role in public safety and how data is managed.
Massachusetts towns like Salem and Cambridge reconsidered Flock contracts due to privacy issues and community pushback.

title: Former Red Sox manager Alex Cora breaks silence on firing, future in baseball
author: Conor Ryan
bullets: Alex Cora was fired by the Red Sox in April after a 10-17 start to the 2026 season.
Cora expressed mixed feelings about his firing, stating relief from job pressures and joy for time with family.
Cora declined a managerial offer from the Phillies and plans to return to managing, but the timeline is uncertain.
